outcome.answer:
Qiao variable length semantic IDs are addressed by VaLiDRec, which proposes variable-length, LLM-aligned semantic identifiers for generative recommendation. VaLiDRec constructs semantic IDs from informative native LLM vocabulary tokens using token importance estimation, semantic-quality-aware pruning, and collision-aware refinement, so identifier lengths adapt to item semantic complexity; it also avoids autoregressive SID generation by reformulating recommendation as token-set prediction with token-level item scoring. [1]

VaLiDRec differs from other variable-length semantic ID approaches by being explicitly LLM-vocabulary-aligned and by eliminating autoregressive SID generation/beam search in favor of token-set prediction. [1] Other works propose variable-length semantic IDs using discrete variational modeling, probabilistic adaptive-length encoding, or learned variable-length tokenization (including popularity-/information-budget-driven length allocation), but they are not presented as LLM-aligned variable-length SIDs in the same way. [2,3]
